role: independent exploration: verify the harness's rule model with the unused budget
hypothesis: Where the parent can go wrong is not the model's query choice (already vetted) but the harness's own reading of the rules: it stops at ~11 queries with every circuit 'SOLVED', yet only ~3-4 of each circuit's 8 rows were observed, and some circuits are 'solved' purely through the inventory-split coupling (e.g. i130 C was pinned by one direct C query). Falsifiable: if that reading is wrong for an instance, spending the leftover queries on the weakest-supported rows (coupling-only distinctions first, then unobserved rows on the least-observed circuit) yields at least one answer that contradicts the 'SOLVED' table; if the reading is right, there are zero contradictions and the final guess is unchanged. Result on this batch: 0 contradictions in ~70 verification answers across 10 instances, so the hypothesis is FALSIFIED here. The parent's rule model held, and the mechanism acts as insurance at no cost to the final table.
behavior_changes: After the rule-derived space pins all three circuits, querying continues to the full budget instead of stopping (queries/ep 11.1 -> 18).

Check menu (the model still picks; off-list or repeated replies are re-asked): first rows where circuits would still differ if each were read on its own without the inventory-split coupling, then any unobserved row, with the least-observed circuit first; each entry shows the table's predicted bit.
In the check phase the state says 'pinned down' instead of 'SOLVED ... Do NOT query again' (first run had that conflict and extra re-asks, e.g. i130 23 -> 20 calls after fix).

Tiered fallback when answers contradict the joint rule space: per circuit, rules read on their own (no exact split) -> any non-constant table consistent with answers, ranked by Hamming closeness to a rule-allowed table (parent fell straight to 'any table', unranked, for all circuits).
preserved_behaviors: Same joint candidate enumeration, entropy-ranked query menu, and query vetting during the main phase.
Model writes every query; harness never chooses one.
Final 24 bits assembled from the model's numbered picks among consistent candidates.
Label-free: only env.query answers and the system-prompt rules are used; no instance/index branching.
verification: Ran check_b1r0_cand_pilot_strict_b10g3r2_b1r0g1.py twice (before/after the 'SOLVED' wording fix): 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, queries_used=18, 0 crashes.

Label-free consistency check from the run's own answers: every final guess agrees with all 18 observed answers; every guess is identical to the parent's guess on the same instance; the parent's guesses also agree with all ~70 new verification answers (0 contradictions); the relaxed/fallback space was never entered.
Direct coverage rose from ~11/24 to 18/24 rows per episode (5-8 rows observed per circuit).

Offline mock (a scripted picker, not the 7B) with off-rule circuits (XOR-like A table; an allocation violating the inventory split): the fallback recovered the exact 24 bits in all 3 cases; a rule-consistent case was unchanged.
risks: On this batch the change made no difference to the final guesses; its value only shows if the rule reading is wrong for some instances in the wider distribution.
About 7 extra model calls per episode (more tokens and latency).
If a contradiction does occur late, the 'any table' tier can leave several unobserved rows for the 7B to choose among from a ranked list. Closeness ranking helps but the pick may still be wrong.
The check menu is ordered by observation count, so the 7B sometimes picks lower-listed checks; harmless because all listed items are unobserved rows.
